data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism claims that preferring better-corroborated theories maximizes falsifiability potential and 'keeps the error-elimination process most active.' But this is internally contradictory: a theory that has survived many severe tests has already had much of its falsifiability potential exhausted — its risky predictions have been checked and confirmed, removing those testable consequences from the pool of open problems. A theory with the highest remaining falsifiability potential is one with many untested risky predictions, which is precisely a less-corroborated theory. So 'better-corroborated' and 'maximizes falsifiability potential' pull in opposite directions. The stated methodological rule (prefer better-corroborated theories) does not achieve its own stated goal (keep error-elimination most active); if anything, the most error-elimination-activating strategy would prefer theories with the most untested empirical content. The target thus fails to establish that its proposed re-framing actually delivers the methodological benefit it invokes to avoid induction.
